title: Rehabilitation pathways for patients with hip or knee prosthesis infections: A European mixed-methods study
summary:
The cross-border research project ‘Functional and psychosocial needs of patients of working age during rehabilitation after periprosthetic infection of the knee or hip joint’ (PJIneeds) aims to develop a rehabilitation support programme that addresses the needs of patients during their rehabilitation after periprosthetic hip/knee joint infection (PJI). This should improve rehabilitation pathways after PJI and optimise postoperative outcomes, enabling patients to achieve their optimal potential in daily life. The entire project consists of four different studies (Study 1 to Study 4). The current registration concerns Study 3 of the overall ‘PJIneeds’ project.
This study is mixed methods, including both a quantitative (survey)  and qualitative part (interviews). This study will be conducted in Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, and the UK. Healthcare professionals involved in the care of patients with a periprosthetic hip or knee joint infection will be included. We aim to determine what differences and similarities there are in addressing patients' (unmet) needs  after PJI in the current rehabilitation pathways between the different countries.
conditions: Healthcare professionals (m/f/d) who are involved in the care of of patients with a periprosthetic hip or knee joint infection (PJI).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthcare professionals involved in the management of patients with knee/hip arthroplasty (e.g., orthopedic surgeons, rehabilitation physicians, physiotherapists, orthopedic nurses) from Germany, The Netherlands, Norway, and the UK.
Exclusion criteria:
Age <18 years; insufficient language skills (depending on recruitment country)
